title: Plan review: quota-aware multi-provider chains and failover (real production plan, seeded defects)

defects.title: Plan misstates the retry replay guard: claims streams replay even after partial assistant output
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that the key_files claim about retry.ts is false: withRetryStream gates replay on whether the attempt already produced evidence (the attemptProducedEvidence guard, proven by tests/unit/orchestration/agent-runtime/shared/llm/llm-errors-retry.test.ts, which the plan itself lists as proof that a stream with emitted evidence is NOT replayed), so chain failover cannot replay unconditionally. Naming only a vague doubt about retry behavior without the evidence-gate mechanism does not count.

defects.title: Live provider availability owner is placed in infra and imports the orchestration Copilot adapter
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that placing src/infra/llm/provider-availability.ts in infra while reusing COPILOT_STATIC_HEADERS and the credential refresh helper from src/orchestration/agent-runtime/llm/copilot.ts inverts the dependency direction (infra imports nothing from src/), so the plan as written fails the module-boundary rule; live availability, model support, and the poll belong in orchestration. Naming the infra placement without the concrete orchestration import that makes it illegal counts only if the boundary rule is stated.

defects.title: Materialized chain-head provider plus automatic flag creates parallel state and hidden pinning
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that persisting a resolved chain-head provider alongside an automatic flag stores a derived value that goes stale (auth changes, availability changes, chain reordering) and effectively pins automatic roles at snapshot time, defeating per-request chain resolution at the client factory; provider omission is the correct representation of automatic selection. Calling out only the extra field without the staleness or hidden-pin consequence does not count.

defects.title: Failover replays mid-stream regardless of already-emitted output, duplicating the partial turn
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that replaying the full request on the next provider after partial assistant text or tool calls have been emitted duplicates or corrupts the turn (tool calls can execute twice), that no UI dedup mechanism exists to drop a replayed prefix, and that the plan's own verbatim user description requires failover only when no durable response evidence has been emitted. The finding must reject the replay-after-evidence design, not merely question the UI-dedup claim.

defects.title: Rate-limit failures advance the chain, contradicting the settled failover trigger
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that treating rate_limit_exceeded as chain-advancing contradicts the authoritative user description embedded in the plan (only terminal quota classes advance the chain; rate limits stay in the existing same-provider retry with retry-after handling) and changes retry semantics for non-quota failures, which the description lists as out of scope. Citing either the embedded spec contradiction or the out-of-scope violation counts; a generic preference for retrying rate limits does not.

defects.title: Schema default 4000 for the Copilot cap makes absent mean capped and writes config at startup
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that a schema-level default of 4000 inverts the settled semantics (field absent = uncapped; 4000 is only a UI prefill), so every user without the setting silently gets Copilot skipped at 4000 credits, and that persisting the defaulted section at startup mutates user config the user never wrote. Catching the absent-means-uncapped inversion is required; the startup write is supporting detail.

defects.title: Quota poll logs the Authorization header, leaking the GitHub token to the log file
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that the phase-3 test scenario requiring the quota poll to log the full outgoing request including the Authorization header value writes a plaintext credential into the global log, violating the Redacted secret-handling policy (unwrap only at the provider-call header, no secret in logs), which the plan elsewhere restates. Vague concern about verbose logging without naming the credential leak does not count.

review_prompt_hint: This is a production implementation plan (plan-handoff JSON) for quota-aware LLM provider chains with in-stream failover, process-local availability tracking, config, and notices. Verify its claims about existing code, its module placement, its state ownership, and its streaming and retry semantics against the codebase and the authoritative user description embedded in the plan
